tool_input.description: Compare the 7de pair with the registered 8a pair

result:
## Findings (all read at 2ee2bd6a)

**No producer/dependency registration exists to update.** Both checkers are mechanical:

- `scripts/walk-topology-audit.py:27-31` derives producers solely from `const TARGET_RELATIVE_PATH = "ratchets/…"` and consumption edges from any `"ratchets/…"` string; unproduced references are allowed as frozen lineage (58-60).
- `scripts/walk-planner-coverage.py:35-40` compares only the literal `LADDER_ORDER` list. In `new-ci/src/bin/plan.rs`, `LADDER_ORDER` is used just for path mapping (1320-1324) and sort rank (1327-1333); producer resolution is path-based via `resolve_producer` (1053). **So the whole planner change is adding the three names to `LADDER_ORDER` in the same positions.**

**All three are genuine `--write`/`--check` generators** — `h2-6a-map-option-projection.mjs:120`, `h2-7de-candidates.mjs:304`, `h2-7de-observations.mjs:10` — so they belong in ORDER, not on an exception list.

## Exact ORDER insertion (`scripts/chain-walk.sh:135-184`)

```
  h2-6a-witnesses
  h2-6a-qualification
  h2-6a-map-option-projection          # consumes ratchets/h2-6a-qualification.v1.json
  h2-6b-witnesses
  …
  h2-7a-close h2-7b-qualification h2-7c-qualification
  h2-7de-candidates h2-7de-observations h2-7de-qualification
  h2-8a-candidates h2-8a-observations
```

Justification from the scripts themselves: `h2-7de-candidates.mjs` consumes `ratchets/h2-{6c,7b,7c}-qualification.v1.json` and `ratchets/h2-candidate-dispositions.v1.json`, all produced earlier; `h2-7de-observations.mjs:7` imports `sourceCommit, inputPath, inventoryPath, persist` **from** `h2-7de-candidates.mjs` and at lines 12-13 persists those two paths with a hard-coded `"--check"`, so it can never rewrite the candidate inputs and must run after the candidates rung. The placement mirrors the already-registered `h2-8a-candidates h2-8a-observations` pair. Mirror the identical sequence into `LADDER_ORDER` (plan.rs:32+).

## Your two specific questions

**Inventory cannot be clobbered.** `--inventory` is a third mode that writes `docs/design/greenfield/slices/h2-6a-map-option-inventory.json` (map-option-projection lines 17, 122-124); `--write`/`--check` touch only `crates/compiler/tests/fixtures/h2-6a-map-option-projection.json` (16, 127-128). The driver invokes `node "$script" --check` (chain-walk.sh:386) and `--write` in the mint phase — never `--inventory`. Registering the rung is therefore safe; the historical inventory stays a deliberate manual action.

**Frozen `source_commit` does not react to a walk.** It is a hardcoded literal, `export const sourceCommit = "050880ce…"` at `h2-7de-candidates.mjs:10`, imported by the observations script — exactly the pattern of the already-walked `h2-8a-candidates.mjs:10`. `--write` reproduces the same bytes, so no churn and no pin invalidation. The 8a pair is the working precedent.

## Risks

1. **Audit blind spot, not an inversion.** None of the three declares `TARGET_RELATIVE_PATH`, so `producer_of` records nothing for them and their outputs (`ratchets/h2-7de-candidates.v1.json`, `-candidate-inputs.v1.json`, `-observations.v1.json`, and the compiler fixture) are treated as frozen lineage. Their self-references are consequently allowed rather than exempted, so adding them will not trip the audit — but the audit will not *enforce* their position against future consumers either. Adding the const would fix that; it would also change each generator's bytes, and both scripts embed `generator: identity("crates/oracle/…")` in their artifacts, so it would force a metadata-only re-mint of three artifacts plus their consumer pins. **Do not do that in this slice** — record it as a known blind spot and let the placement be enforced by review until a slice that is already re-minting those artifacts.
2. `ratchets/h2-candidate-dispositions.v1.json` is produced by `h2-transition.mjs:15` under `CANDIDATE_RELATIVE_PATH`, which `TARGET_PATTERN` does not match — same blind-spot class. Harmless here (h2-transition is position 7), but it means that edge is unverified.
3. `plan.rs:1320-1324` filters `LADDER_ORDER` by scanned node paths, so a name present in the list but absent from the scan is silently dropped there while `walk-planner-coverage.py` still demands literal equality. Keep the two lists byte-identical in sequence, not just as sets.
4. Placing `h2-6a-map-option-projection` before `h2-6a-qualification` would be a real inversion and the audit will catch it — the one ordering the mechanical check does enforce for these three.

## Structural test before the sanctioned walk

`WALK_DRY=1 bash scripts/chain-walk.sh` — it stops after preflight plus all three self-checks (coverage at chain-walk.sh:199-212, planner at 217, topology at 221), which is exactly the harness for an ORDER edit and requires no mint. Complement with `python3 scripts/walk-topology-audit.py --self-test` and the existing `gate-tax-5.test.mjs`. Expect the coverage line to read 68 rather than 65 chain scripts after the edit.

No finished claim: this covers the ORDER/planner registration only, the real walk is still unrun, and the full unsplit CI remains required.
